maria: FYI saw a sharp p99 spike during the overnight load test (~03:12 UTC). timeline matches a burst of long-sequence requests and a flurry of paged-KV page-ins. batcher ended up grouping several long reqs, FlashAttention dropped out and we paid kernel-init + pagebackpressure costs. sharing a tiny log excerpt below.

kevin: can you paste the relevant logs/traces or a perf flame? even a trimmed batcher log helps.

maria: batcher.log (trimmed):
```
[03:12:13] batch_open id=0x9f3 active_reqs=51 total_tokens=1980 token_budget=2048
[03:12:14] paged_kv: page_ins=104 page_in_ms_avg=13.8
[03:12:14] kernel_switch: from=flash to=hybrid reason=paged_kv_pressure
[03:12:14] batch_close latency_ms=438
```

li: repro steps I used locally: start the continuous-batcher with the longseq-spike profile (seq ~1000) and paged-kv enabled. command:
```
./run_local.sh --config configs/continuous-batcher.yaml --profile longseq-spike
perf record -g -- ./bin/continuous-batcher --workload=longseq-spike
```
I captured perf during the surge window.

ethan: I ran into a similar incident last week. root causes look like: (1) batch formation doesn't degrade per-request token allocation when KV page-ins ramp, so a few long requests can consume most of the batch token quota; (2) kernel selection is eager to fallback off FlashAttention when paged-kv crosses thresholds, causing expensive kernel swaps + cold init overhead.

kevin: proposal: adaptive per-request token cap + smoothing. when paged_kv.fault_rate > TH, cap token_target per-request to something like min(default_target, tokens_remaining / active_long_reqs) with an exponential smoothing window. should avoid single long reqs dominating the batch.

maria: sample config I tried (pseudo-yaml):
```
batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  per_request_token_policy: adaptive
  adaptive:
    paged_kv_fault_rate_threshold: 0.015
    fallback_per_request_target: 80
    smoothing_alpha: 0.3
```

li: short local numbers (16-GPU emulation, synthetic KV faults):
- baseline (no adaptive): p95 = 380ms, p99 = 1150ms, throughput = 440 rps
- adaptive per-request cap: p95 = 240ms, p99 = 510ms, throughput = 405 rps
So p99 improved a lot; throughput dropped ~8% but tails look acceptable for our SLOs.

ethan: + another improvement: kernel-swap hysteresis. if we flip kernels because of a transient paged-kv spike, don't immediately flip back for the next N batches. this prevents oscillation and repeated init costs. i added a tiny rate limiter and saw swap_count drop dramatically.

kevin: code sketch for hysteresis:
```
if (should_swap && swaps_in_window < swap_limit) { swap(); swaps_in_window++; } else { keep_current_kernel(); }
// reset swaps_in_window after hysteresis_window_ms
```

maria: agree with canary plan: land adaptive token cap first, then enable kernel.swap_hysteresis. test them independently then together.

ops-bot: deploy request created: deploy/eng-runtime/canary/1887654321 -> targets: canary-pool-4, rollout=15%

li: I'll run the canary and collect traces. plan flags: `batcher.adaptive_per_request=true` and `kernel.swap_hysteresis=4`. will attach perf samples and dashboard screenshots.
